I Want to Love Linux. It Doesn’t Love Me Back: Post 2 – The Audio Stack Is a Crime Scene
Published on
May 12, 2025
You Can’t Hear Anything—and It’s Not Your Fault
You plug in headphones.
Nothing.
You unplug them again.
Still nothing.
The speakers are muted.
The system says they aren’t.
You check volumes. You restart Pulse. You restart PipeWire.
You restart your whole damn session.
And still—
no sound.
That’s just a Tuesday on Linux audio.
Sometimes the device shows up and just won’t play anything.
Sometimes it does—but stutters constantly like it's on a failing cassette tape.
Sometimes laptop speakers never work at all unless you run a six-line
hda-verb
incantation copied from a 9-year-old mailing list post.
Sometimes, the system boots up with everything at 0% volume.
Why?
Because PulseAudio once had a patch to mute sound on boot.
Then someone reverted that patch because it was breaking things.
Then someone re-applied it.
Then someone re-reverted it.
Then someone added a workaround that cancels the revert of the unmute of the mute.
This is real. This is production. This is Linux audio.
A Brief History of This Disaster
It started simple.
ALSA was the kernel-level driver layer: Advanced Linux Sound Architecture.
It’s still here.
It still runs the hardware.
But back in the early 2000s, people realized ALSA wasn’t enough. It couldn’t mix audio from multiple sources. It couldn’t route sound across apps. It was raw, low-level, and unforgiving.
So we got
PulseAudio
.
It was supposed to be the layer on top of ALSA—handling device routing, per-app volume control, hotplug support, etc.
Except it was buggy. And laggy. And didn’t always work.
But everything depended on it.
Fast forward to now: Pulse is deprecated in favor of
PipeWire
—and this time, it’s actually good.
PipeWire, together with
WirePlumber
(not
pipewire-media-session
), finally gives us a modern, low-latency, graph-based audio and video system. Bluetooth profiles? Handled. Device routing? Solid. Policy control? Configurable. It fixes real problems that PulseAudio never could.
But here's the problem:
the software ecosystem hasn't caught up.
Most apps still expect Pulse. They talk to
pipewire-pulse
, the compatibility layer—not PipeWire itself.
The stack is clean. The interfaces are better. But the expectations are still stuck in 2012.
And for blind users, that matters. Because even with PipeWire working beautifully, we still hit problems like:
Device indexes aren’t simple numbers anymore—they’re long UUID-like IDs, which makes scripting harder.
Audio is still tied to your user session. That means root can’t speak—just like with Pulse.
Tools like
espeakup
or
fenrir
still require config hacks to forward audio from root to your user via WirePlumber.
So yes—PipeWire is a massive improvement. But the legacy Pulse model still shapes how software behaves, and the new stack inherits the same fundamental issue:
your sound only works if your user session works.
And that’s the exact point where blind users often lose access.
And even beyond that:
You still need Pulse for legacy apps.
You still need ALSA for direct hardware access.
You still need JACK for pro audio tools that never moved on.
So the result? A modern core surrounded by the same old mess.
Debugging Hell: Audio Edition
When audio breaks on Linux, it doesn’t crash.
It doesn’t throw a friendly dialog.
It doesn’t log anything useful.
You just… don’t get sound.
You start running commands:
pactl
list
sinks
pactl
list
sources
alsamixer
systemctl
--user
status
pipewire
journalctl
-xe
Maybe you see a device. Maybe not.
Maybe it shows up as “dummy output.”
Maybe it shows up as working—while emitting nothing.
If you're lucky,
pavucontrol
shows the wrong profile and you can fix it.
If you're unlucky, there's no fix. Or the fix doesn’t persist. Or the profile isn't even listed.
Sometimes PipeWire crashes and restarts.
Sometimes it doesn't.
Sometimes Pulse is still running and you didn’t notice.
Sometimes
two
instances of PipeWire are running—because of a race between your display manager and your session manager.
Sometimes Bluetooth just doesn’t work unless you restart the service in exactly the right order with a magic D-Bus incantation.
Sometimes your speakers disappear when you unplug headphones.
Sometimes they come back muted.
Sometimes you
unmute them and they still don’t play
—because Pulse remembered a per-port volume of zero from 3 years ago.
And this is just normal desktop audio.
Firmware, UCM, and the Dark Corners
Now let’s talk about laptops.
Not desktops.
Not audio interfaces.
Laptops.
Because here, you get firmware bugs and undocumented quirks.
Your speakers might not work unless you boot with
snd-hda-intel.model=laptop
.
Or
dell-headset-multi
.
Or maybe
auto
.
Or maybe that breaks your microphone.
You’ll find a forum post that says:
“Add a
~/.asoundrc
file with these three lines.”
And maybe that works.
Or maybe it breaks
every other
audio device.
Then there’s UCM—Use Case Manager.
Not document
43963288.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Linux音频系统的复杂性和常见问题。作者描述了在Linux上使用音频设备时遇到的种种困扰，例如插入耳机没有声音、设备显示为“虚拟输出”、音量设置无法保存等。这些问题源于音频栈的演变历史：从早期的ALSA到问题多多的PulseAudio，再到现代的PipeWire。虽然PipeWire在技术上更为先进，解决了PulseAudio的许多问题，但由于软件生态尚未完全适配，许多应用程序仍然依赖PulseAudio，导致兼容性问题。此外，ALSA和JACK等旧系统仍需使用，使得音频调试变得更加复杂。文章还提到，在笔记本电脑上，固件问题和未记录的 quirks 使得音频故障更加难以解决。总体而言，Linux音频系统虽然有所改进，但依然存在诸多挑战。

data.title: Traffic Fatalities Are a Choice
data.author: mitchbob
data.article_summary: 文章指出，美国道路交通死亡率高企并非不可避免，而是政策选择的结果。美国的交通死亡率是每10万人12.8人，远高于许多发达国家。2022年，超过42,000人死于交通事故。相比之下，荷兰、瑞典等国家通过实施“安全系统”方法显著降低了死亡率。该方法承认人为驾驶错误难以避免，因此通过城市规划和道路设计来引导更安全的行为，例如通过物理隔离和限速来减少严重碰撞。荷兰的“Stop de Kindermoord”运动推动了道路安全改革，实施了分离自行车道和“生活街道”（woonerf）等设计。通过系统性变革，荷兰在1998至2008年间大幅降低了交通事故死亡率。美国若采取类似措施，本可避免大量死亡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：改善道路设计与交通安全的多方面考量，包括自动驾驶、超速监控、年龄因素等。

不同观点：
• **道路设计与多方受益**（zamalek）：认为改善道路设计（如缩窄人行横道、移除路口停车）能使驾驶员和行人双赢。通过增加驾驶员之间的可见性，所有人都能从中受益，而非简单的零和博弈。

• **年龄对交通事故的影响**（oicu812）：指出即使在荷兰这样的国家，70岁以上老年人的交通事故死亡率仍较高，认为仅靠道路设计不足以解决问题，还需要提升年轻人和老年人的驾驶技能。

• **其他事故原因**（imglorp）：提到美国每年因酒驾、分心驾驶、疲劳驾驶导致的死亡人数显著，认为自动驾驶汽车有可能减少这些事故。

• **超速与车辆类型问题**（benabbott）：认为宽阔平坦的道路让驾驶员难以判断速度，驾驶大型车辆（如SUV）的人更易紧跟其他车辆，增加风险。支持广泛使用超速摄像头，但指出需要改变道路设计和车辆类型。

• **统计指标的争议**（engine_y, stellalo）：质疑文章中使用的死亡率统计指标，建议应按每公里死亡率或事故率来衡量，以更准确反映实际情况。

• **自动驾驶的未来作用**（xnx, delichon）：认为自动驾驶（如Waymo）可能在减少未来交通事故死亡方面发挥更大作用，主张在进行大规模基础设施改善时应考虑自动驾驶技术的快速发展。

• **超速摄像头的可行性与隐私问题**（psunavy03）：认为超速摄像头的设置需基于合理的限速，且涉及市政收入和隐私问题。

补充讨论：
• **各国交通事故的可比性**（semiinfinitely）：质疑美国与一些国家在交通事故死亡率上的直接对比，认为基于国情不同，可能不具备可比性。

• **交通安全行为选择**（zahlman, giantg2）：讨论交通问题是否是个人选择的结果，并争论是否存在唯一正确的选择。

• **城市规划的未来**（ChicagoDave）：建议城市应规划独立的自动驾驶车道、自行车道和人行道，以减少伤害、燃料消耗和污染。

• **安全带与头盔的使用**（red_admiral）：对不系安全带和不戴头盔的行为表示不解，强调这些基本安全措施的重要性。

争议焦点：改善道路设计与提升驾驶技能、自动驾驶技术的未来作用、超速监控的实施与隐私问题、以及如何合理衡量交通事故死亡率。

43964304.article_content:
Traffic Fatalities Are a Choice
Abi Olvera
America’s roads are more dangerous than those of almost every country in the developed world. We know how to change that.
You are as likely to die driving on an American road as you are driving in Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan. The American traffic-related death rate ranks 87th in the world. At 12.8 deaths per 100,000 people, it is double that of Greece, triple that of Austria, and six times more than Japan. In 2022, more than 42,000 people died on American roads, and more than two million — 1 in every 170 — required emergency medical care from automobile-related accidents. The total economic cost, in medical expenses and loss of life, amounted to an estimated $470 billion.
This is not an inevitability. It is a policy decision that the federal and state governments continue to affirm. Indeed, if the United States had matched the rate of improvement in road safety since the 1970s seen in, for example, the Netherlands, Sweden, or Spain, it would have prevented 2 out of every 3 road deaths, saving 25,000 lives last year alone.
It’s tempting to argue — and some do — that such drastic reductions are easier to accomplish in small, dense, European countries. But even relatively car-centric countries like Britain, Canada, and Australia cut road deaths by nearly half between 1979 and 2002. In the United States, they decreased by just
16% over the same time
.
What did Sweden, Spain, and other countries do that the US did not? Each of the countries that reduced their road deaths used the same method: they implemented a set of urban planning decisions — and a philosophy which informs them — now called the
Safe System
approach.
Safe System origins
At its core, the Safe System approach acknowledges that human error while driving is inevitable. Thus, road designers and urban planners should engineer environments to guide safer behaviors. Smart design ensures that when human error happens, it does not lead to severe crashes by, for example, physically separating pedestrians from high speed car traffic, and by designing roads that don’t facilitate high speeds.
The philosophy traces its origins to road safety activism that first began in the Netherlands in the 1970s. The Netherlands at that time had a road fatality rate 15% higher than that of the United States. It reached an apex in 1971, when more than 3,300 people, including more than 400 children,were killed in driving accidents — a fatality rate equivalent to 25 per 100,000 people. Out of public outrage was born the
Stop de Kindermoord
or Stop the Child Murder movement, spearheaded by bereaved parents and civil society organizations who demanded safer streets across the country.
Activists within
Stop de Kindermoord
were pragmatic. They worked with urban planners and local communities to develop innovative, safer street designs. One result was the separated bicycle tracks for which the Netherlands is now famous. So, too, was a new street design known as
woonerf
, or
living street
, which used physical elements like bends, curves, and trees to deliberately slow traffic and provided for shared space between pedestrians, cars, and bicycles.
Through continued activism — and partially aided by the oil crisis of 1974, which made driving less economically attractive — many designs were taken up by politicians who
codified new rules
on street design, funding, and governance. Over decades, the Netherlands continued to improve its road design, pioneering the behavioral-engineering approach. For example, the Dutch developed the concept of “
self-explaining
” roads, which intuitively guide drivers to safe speeds via engineering features.
Yet progress was not linear. Many road improvements were implemented in
more piecemeal fashion
, not country-wide but neighborhood by neighborhood, city by city. After early success, reductions in road fatalities stalled through the 1980s. Recognizing the need to catalyze further change, in the late 1980s, the Dutch States General set an ambitious goal: a 50% reduction in road deaths by 2010.
To meet those goals, the Netherlands enacted what is
cited
as the very first “system approach” to road safety — the Dutch then called it “Sustainable Safety” — which applied three principles to road design that look like an early version of today’s conception of Safe System: a hierarchical network of road types, each with its own design and speed limits; “homogeneity,” which uses speed management and directional separation to manage interactions between vehicles of different masses; and predictability for drivers via consistent design principles.
These changes required a massive implementation program. Between 1998 and 2008, for instance, the percentage of roads in Dutch cities that were zoned at 30 km/h increased from 15% to 70%, while the percentage of rural roads zoned at 80km/h dropped from 97% to 43%. Over the same time period, fatality rates dropped steadily — 5.3% per year — compared to only 1.8% in the preceding 10

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：创伤叙事在当代文学中的使用及其影响

不同观点：
• 一些读者认为，当今使用创伤叙事的作家过度关注创伤，而缺乏积极的元素，如美好的结局、希望或对未来的信仰。这种过度关注创伤的情节可能让读者感到压抑。
• 另一种观点则指出，创伤和苦难本身并不特殊，创伤叙事不必通过让角色的苦难显得特殊来传达希望和信仰。即使在描绘苦难时，作品也可以生成希望和信仰。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到的"幸福结局"和"希望"是与创伤叙事相对立的元素，表明读者渴望在文学作品中看到平衡，即创伤与希望的并存。
• 争议的焦点在于创伤叙事的表现方式：是否应该通过强调角色的特殊性来激发读者的共鸣和希望，还是通过其他方式如普遍的人类经验来传达希望。
• 例子中隐含了对文学作品社会功能的讨论，即文学是否应该主要反映现实的痛苦，还是更应提供一种超越痛苦的视角。

data.title: Fan Service
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文描述了在OpenBSD系统上为ASUS笔记本开发ACPI WMI驱动以控制风扇速度的过程。ASUS笔记本通过Fn键组合可以调节风扇速度，但该功能在OpenBSD上不可用。作者首先解释了ACPI作为硬件抽象层的作用，并指出虽然ACPI提供了标准方法，但厂商常加入非标准功能，导致仍需编写自定义驱动。作者试图通过WMI扩展解决此问题，WMI使用GUID映射方法名以识别特定功能。

作者开发了一个初步的ACPI驱动读取_WDG缓冲区并修正GUID字节顺序问题。通过分析系统ACPI代码，解决了调用_WED方法时返回值恒为1的问题，成功识别不同事件。进一步编写代码处理设备状态，成功控制键盘背光灯，但在调节风扇模式时未见效果。参考Linux驱动后，发现需要进行位操作以检测和设置风扇状态，但仍未获得预期结果，推测可能遗漏了Linux驱动中的某些细节。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕现代计算机系统中ACPI、WMI、EC（嵌入式控制器）等技术在功能实现上的变化及其影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• [userbinator] 认为，过去在EC中实现的功能（如屏幕亮度、音量调整等）在任何操作系统下都能正常工作，甚至在DOS中也不需要驱动程序。然而，现代笔记本电脑需要依赖复杂的操作系统和驱动程序来实现这些简单功能，这是一种倒退和生态封闭的表现，可能是微软希望通过这种方式增加PC生态系统的封闭性。

• [mjg59] 指出，Windows通过WMI让用户空间的策略代理更容易接入，而不是直接调用原始的ACPI方法。尽管WMI在某种程度上是自描述的，但很多方法并没有文档记录，因此仍需要通过反编译ACPI字节码来理解。这表明WMI的复杂性和文档不足带来了额外的技术挑战。

• [diegoperini] 对Linux系统中代码结构的有序性表示赞赏，但也指出其逻辑性虽然强，但使用起来并不那么方便，形象地比喻为在按字母顺序排列的超市中导航。

• [ac29] 提到电池寿命的改善以及通过设置EPB来实现更高效的CPU频率调节，从而降低风扇噪音。这表明在Linux系统中，通过技术手段可以实现更高的能效和更好的用户体验。

• [dodomodo] 认为，ACPI WMI的设计初衷是让固件能够更直接地暴露高级WMI对象，这比Linux中的sysfs风格更清晰易用。然而，当支持的基础设施不足时，这种设计的优势就不再明显。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了技术实现的历史变化，以及这种变化对用户体验和系统复杂性的影响。
• 对Linux和Windows系统中不同技术方案的优缺点进行了对比，特别是WMI和sysfs风格的对比。
• 涉及了技术文档的缺乏和技术实现的复杂性对开发者和用户的影响。
• 对现代系统中功能实现的封闭性和复杂性提出了批评，并讨论了这种趋势可能带来的生态系统封闭问题。

43951368.article_content:
fan service
ASUS laptops generally have a feature that lets the user toggle the fan speed. Fn-F5 on some models, Fn-F on others. The direct effect is to limit the fan speed, from whisper mode to megablast, and indirectly control performance. But it doesn’t work in OpenBSD, so I needed to write an ASUS ACPI WMI driver.
acpi
ACPI is a hardware abstraction layer that lets the computer tell the operating system how to do things. It provides functions in byte code which the OS interprets to perform certain tasks. So instead of having to write a driver for every CPU, you call the ACPI method _PSS and that tells you what to do.
Of course, vendors want to include functionality that isn’t defined in the standard, so they add some extra methods, and then you end up writing some custom drivers anyway, for the little buttons that turn the microphone on and off, etc. OpenBSD (and other OSs) have lots of little drivers for ThinkPads and whatnot.
ACPI method names are only four letters long, so what do we do if two vendors include a method called WMNB and how do we determine what it does? (Technically, the ACPI nodes are identified by seven letter names, and the methods live under them, so it’s not really a problem, but somebody got paid to make a solution anyway.)
wmi
The solution is an extension to ACPI called WMI, which stands for Windows Multiplies Irritations or something. You ask ACPI for a buffer called _WDG, and this contains a table mapping GUIDs (globally unique, says so right there in the name) to local method names. Looking through this table, we come across
DCBA-FE-10-23-456789
, which we recognize as a GUID of interest, and this tells us the method to call is WMNB, but now we know it’s the right one.
OpenBSD does not have a WMI driver, which is part of what I need to set the fan profile. There is a WMI driver in Linux, and it includes an ASUS support driver for a variety of functions I’m interested in.
first steps
First, I wrote a little acpi driver that attaches to PNP0C14. Read the _WDG buffer and print out all the GUIDs. Didn’t recognize any of the values, then realized I got the byte order wrong. Fixed that, saw something very close, realized I still didn’t get the byte order quite right. GUIDs are not big endian, they are not little endian, they are Goldilocks endian.
With that sorted out, I was able to enable events and get a printf every time I pushed a hotkey.
events
After receiving an interrupt and landing in our callback, we need to identify which event just happened by calling _WED. I did this, but was only getting 1 in response every time, regardless of key. I was a little stuck here. Very close to getting what I wanted, but without much clue as to what went wrong.
Turns out you can just look at your system’s ACPI code. OpenBSD runs
acpidump
at boot and saves all the files. Copy them to a work directory, run
iasl -d
, and have a look. A quick grep for _WED reveals the source.
Method (_WED, 1, NotSerialized)
{
If ((Arg0 == 0xFF))
{
Return (GANQ ())
}
Return (One)
}
Method (GANQ, 0, Serialized)
{
P8XH (Zero, 0xF2)
If (AQNO)
{
AQNO--
Local0 = DerefOf (ATKQ [AQHI])
AQHI++
AQHI &= 0x0F
Return (Local0)
}
Return (Ones)
}
Even without knowing anything at all about ASL, this looks like a function that dequeues an event, but only if called with an argument of 255. That was the bug! Once I called it with the correct argument, I started receiving different event codes for backlight toggle, fan toggle, AC attach, etc.
devices
Wrote some more code to handle getting and setting device state. There’s a magic incantation to call an ACPI method and pass it a device id, which could be the keyboard backlight, or the wifi led, or the fan profile, etc. Started with the keyboard backlight, since this was pretty easy to observe.
After fixing a few simple bugs like reversing the device ids for fnlock and backlight, I was able to blink the keyboard light by pressing F7. It’s all coming together.
Toggling the fan profile didn’t seem to accomplish anything, though. Under Windows, there is an audible difference switching to whisper mode, but I didn’t observe any change.
The Linux driver includes code for at least three different fan and performance profile settings. The same driver is used for a wide range of laptops, from thin and lights to gaming fraggers. According to the Linux driver, you can detect which devices are present by reading their state, then checking for a high bit, and then getting the value by masking off some low bits. This seemed to indicate I had a fan boost device, but it wasn’t responding to my changes.
After printing out the raw values, I noticed they were all -2. That doesn’t seem very likely. But it definitely has a high bit set, and masking off the low bits made it look reasonable. I think I missed something in the Linux driver? There’s lots of shifts and masks in lots of places.
Back to the ACPI dump, the WMNB method is a giant switch statement that ends with  Return (0xFFFFFFFE). So sure enough,

43950976.article_content:
Leaving Google
I’ve left Google after working there for 19 years.
For most of that time I’ve been fortunate in being able to work on the
Go programming language
. Go was started by Rob Pike, Ken Thompson, and Robert Griesemer in the fall of 2007. I joined the team in June, 2008, about the same time as Russ Cox. I’ve been very lucky to be able to work with such remarkable people on such an interesting project.
I am astonished at how much use Go has gotten over the years. Go has reached the status of being just another programming language, one that any programmer can choose when appropriate. That is far beyond what any of us expected in the early days, when our best hope was that Go might serve as an example for useful ideas that other languages and programming environments could adopt.
I started on Go by adding a Go frontend to the
GCC compiler
. The Go project already had a compiler, of course, based on the Inferno C compiler. Having two compilers helped ensure that the language was clearly defined. When the two compilers differed, we knew that we had to clarify the spec and figure out what the right behavior should be.
In general my self-appointed role on the Go team consisted of tracking everything I could about the project and looking for areas that needed help. Among other things in the earlier years I added Go support to Google’s internal build system, and to
the SWIG tool
. For a couple of years I was the team manager. From the first days of Go people asked for support for some sort of generics or type parameterization; working with Robert Griesemer I developed a series of language change proposals, and generics were added to the language in the
Go 1.18 release in 2022
.
My approach had its good points and its bad points. I was quick to see the problems that people were running into today, and the problems they would run into tomorrow, and I was often able to get those problems addressed. But I was slow to see the ideas that would help people do new things that they weren’t trying to do and thus weren’t missing, things such as the Go module proxy and the Go vulnerability database.
Overall I think my approach was a good one in helping to build a successful project. But Gooogle has changed, and Go has changed, and the overall computer programming environment has changed. It’s become clear over the last year or so that I am no longer a good fit for the Go project at Google. I have to move on.
I’m still interested in Go. I don’t think that the language is done. I don’t think that any programming language is ever done–the programming environment changes all the time, and languages must evolve or die. That is doubly true for a language like Go that comes equipped with a substantial standard library, one that must adapt to the new needs of programmers.
I will be taking a break for a while, but I hope to be able to contribute to Go again in the future.
Posted
May 10, 2025
in
Programming
by
Ian Lance Taylor
Tags:
programming
Comments
3 responses to “Leaving Google”
Laurent
May 10, 2025
Dude, fantastic work on go … but wtf… shame on you for hosting your blog on this ad ridden nightmare of a site… please fix… it’s not a good look
Ian Lance Taylor
May 11, 2025
Yeah, looks like the ads have gotten pretty bad. I’ve disabled the Google Ads plugin. Thanks for mentioning it.
cuishuang
May 11, 2025
I was shocked to see the news — I thought you were just taking a long vacation. And I believe the departure is an immeasurable loss to the Go language and its community.
I’ve often seen your active presence across GitHub, the Go groups, and Gerrit. Your professionalism, patience, and kindness were like a breath of fresh air. Not long ago, I even saw you patiently responding to a student from Iran who was asking how to contribute to Go. In today’s world, where geopolitical tensions and ideological divides are growing, your spirit — transcending nationality and race — is truly admirable.
Several years ago, I started with a simple contribution, something like fixing a typo. Many maintainers were unsure whether it was worth merging, but you encouraged it — saying that even simple contributions can lead to more meaningful ones down the road. Thanks to that encouragement, I later found and fixed bugs in the standard library with your help, and added new features to the toolchain. Those moments remain some of the brightest highlights of my career.
Without Ian, I believe the volume and vitality of code reviews in the Go community might be reduced by an order of magnitude. And without your early encouragement, I might never have developed the curiosity and passion of a “language enthusiast” or ventured into deeper exploration.
Wishing you all the best — and I sincerely hope, after a well-deserved break, we’ll meet again in the Go community.

data.title: The Epochalypse Project
data.author: maxeda
data.article_summary:
《Epochalypse项目：32位时间戳漏洞——我们的数字定时炸弹》文章指出，2038年1月19日，全球数百万敏感的嵌入式和工业计算机系统将因32位时间戳溢出出现异常行为，可能导致医院设备、银行系统、交通控制、电网等关键基础设施出现严重故障。该漏洞源于许多系统使用32位整数表示自1970年以来的秒数，到2038年将溢出并导致时间错误。

与千年虫（Y2K）问题相比，此次问题规模更大、嵌入式系统难以更新、社会对数字基础设施依赖更深，且可能被恶意利用。解决这一全球性挑战需要识别和优先处理关键系统，实施修复，并制定应急计划。时间紧迫，需立即采取行动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：2038年问题（Y2038 bug）的严重性、可利用性、影响范围以及可能的解决方案。

不同观点：
• **对漏洞严重性的质疑**：[perlgeek] 提出，虽然时间同步协议可能被恶意利用，但我们尚未看到大量此类攻击。他质疑该漏洞的实际可利用性和严重性，并试图了解问题的严重程度以及解决方案的稳健性。
• **具体影响不明确**：[Waterluvian] 认为，当前对“不可预测的影响”描述过于模糊，建议通过具体测试结果和故障模式的目录，使问题更加具体化，以便引起组织的重视。
• **历史漏洞实例**：[jsd1982] 分享了一个Y2038 bug的实例，在经典ASP代码中遇到该问题，并指出即使错误发生在2038年最大日期14年之前，系统仍然崩溃。这表明遗留代码中可能存在不可预见的问题。
• **对普通用户影响不大**：[AndrewDucker] 认为，对于普通家庭用户而言，要求他们检查智能设备是否能在13年后继续使用是过度要求，因为这些设备很可能不会使用那么久。但企业和基础设施需要注意此问题。
• **解决方案的复杂性**：[johnklos] 强调了解决方案的复杂性，特别是开源项目和企业对于旧系统支持的意愿问题。他提到NetBSD早在2012年就解决了64位时间问题，而Linux的过渡则较为缓慢。他还指出，企业通常不愿投入资源解决旧系统问题。

补充讨论：
• **时间表示范围的广泛性**：[ks2048] 开玩笑地提到未来292271025015年的问题，暗示时间表示范围的问题可能会在极远的未来再次出现。
• **实际修复情况**：[ninjin] 指出OpenBSD在2014年已经修复了Y2038问题，Linux大约在2020年跟进。
• **物联网设备的可弃性**：[Retr0id] 担心许多物联网设备可能只会通过“丢弃旧设备并购买新设备”来解决2038年问题。
• **提高意识的时机**：[sans_souse] 开玩笑地问是否现在提出Y10k问题为时过早，暗示对长远未来的潜在问题不必过早担忧。

争议焦点：
• **漏洞的实际严重性和可利用性**：[perlgeek] 质疑2038年问题的实际可利用性和严重性，并提出为何我们尚未看到大量此类攻击。这表明在社区中对该问题的实际威胁程度存在一定争议。

技术讨论：
• **时间表示的技术细节**：[panzi] 讨论了JavaScript中自Unix纪元以来的毫秒数何时不再能被IEEE双精度浮点数准确表示的问题。
• **具体修复工具和方法**：[mkj] 分享了一个测量软件包中可疑时间转换的工具，并提供了具体的技术实现方法链接。

幽默与轻松话题：
• **时间旅行的玩笑**：[rkapsoro] 开玩笑说计划在2038年举办派对，而[cranberryturkey] 则提到过去曾有人遗憾错过Y2K问题的趣闻。

总结：社区对2038年问题的严重性、影响范围、技术解决方案以及长远未来可能出现的时间表示问题进行了广泛讨论，同时夹杂着一些幽默与轻松的评论。

43952714.article_content:
The Epochalypse Project
The 32-bit Timestamp Vulnerability: Our Digital Time Bomb
On 2038-01-19 03:14:08 UTC, millions of sensitive embedded and industrial computer systems worldwide will suddenly start behaving in unpredictable ways, unless we take coordinated action now. And what’s worse, with unsecured time protocols, attackers don’t need to wait until 2038.
This is not science fiction. It’s a real technical vulnerability affecting systems we rely on daily—from hospital equipment to power grids, from banking systems to transportation networks. This vulnerability is embedded in the fundamental architecture of our digital infrastructure.
Why Should You Care?
Without proper preparation, we will face widespread disruptions including:
Hospital equipment displaying incorrect medication times
Banking systems failing to process payments
Traffic control systems malfunctioning
Power grid instabilities causing outages
Internet service disruptions
Security systems generating false alarms
In our interconnected world, these technical failures could have cascading effects. Critical system failures can endanger lives, disrupt economies, and compromise essential services.
And what’s worse, malicious threat actors can manipulate time synchronization protocols in many cases to trigger this vulnerability at the time of their choosing.
This is particularly concerning given how little attention many networks pay to their Network Time Protocol (NTP) security.
Understanding the 32-bit Timestamp Vulnerability
Many computer systems track time using a 32-bit signed integer that counts seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z (known as “Unix time”). This approach has a mathematical limitation: when this counter reaches its maximum value on 2038-01-19 03:14:08 UTC, affected systems will roll over to negative numbers, causing them to interpret the date as 1901-12-13T20:45:52Z.
This vulnerability exists in:
Legacy systems running critical infrastructure
Embedded devices in industrial settings
Internet of Things (IoT) devices
Transportation and energy management systems
Medical equipment
Financial transaction processors
Telecommunications infrastructure
Millions of “smart” devices in homes and businesses worldwide
The Scale Is Unprecedented
The 32-bit timestamp vulnerability is definitively more severe than Y2K for several critical reasons:
Massive Scale
: There are now hundreds of times more vulnerable systems than existed during Y2K. For the last 30 years, simple controller computers have been embedded into virtually everything that moves or connects.
Embedded Nature
: Unlike Y2K, which primarily affected visible software that could be patched, today’s vulnerability exists in countless embedded systems that cannot be easily updated. Many are physically inaccessible, buried in infrastructure or sealed in hardware.
Increased Dependence
: Our society’s dependence on digital infrastructure has increased dramatically since 2000. Critical systems from healthcare to transportation now rely entirely on accurate timestamps for basic operations.
Security Implications
: The near-universal connectivity of today’s systems means time-related vulnerabilities can be exploited remotely. Unsecured time protocols mean attackers could potentially trigger failures at will.
Less Visibility
: Many vulnerable systems operate without user interfaces or monitoring capabilities, making detection of problems significantly harder than with Y2K.
A Global Challenge
Our digital infrastructure resembles an interconnected ecosystem. When individual components fail simultaneously, the entire system becomes vulnerable. Even if only 15-30% of critical systems fail, we will experience significant disruptions across multiple sectors.
The challenge is compounded by what economists call a “tragedy of the commons”—where responsibility is distributed but no single entity feels accountable for solving the shared problem. Organizations often assume:
“Our systems represent only a small fraction of the infrastructure”
“Other stakeholders will address the critical components”
“Updating legacy systems offers minimal return on investment”
One of the most concerning aspects involves security infrastructure. When system clocks suddenly jump backward, security certificates will become invalid across large portions of the internet, compromising our digital security framework.
Time is Limited, Action is Required
With approximately 12 years remaining until the critical date, we must prioritize our response.
Our analysis indicates we cannot replace or update all vulnerable systems in time. Many embedded devices cannot be updated at all. However, through coordinated action, we can:
Identify and prioritize the most critical vulnerable systems
Implement fixes where possible
Develop contingency plans for systems that cannot be updated
Establish global coordination to manage the transition
Who We Are
The Epochalypse Project was founded by Trey Darley (aka “treyka”) and Pedro Umbelino (aka “kripthor”)

data.title: A conversation about AI for science with Jason Pruet
data.author: LAsteNERD
data.article_summary:
Jason Pruet，洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室国家安全AI办公室主任，讨论了人工智能（AI）在科学和安全领域的未来。五年前，他认为AI只是一种有价值的工具，但随着大型AI模型能力的提升，他现在认为AI将广泛颠覆科学研究方式。AI不再只是工具，而是科学家解决问题和做出发现的基本转变。当前全球竞争的焦点是如何利用AI的潜力，同时减轻其潜在危害。

Pruet将当前的AI发展与二战后的科学支持模式相比较，强调政府需投资AI基础设施以促进公共利益。洛斯阿拉莫斯正通过如Venado（拥有2500个GPU的机器）等项目，与大学合作，提供大规模计算资源。这种合作对于国家安全和能源主导权至关重要。

近年来，AI的快速进展得益于2017年提出的transformer架构，它使得模型规模和性能大幅提升，并能处理多种信息类型。Pruet的观点因此转变，认为政府需大规模投资AI。目前，AI的发展轨迹尚不完全明确，但其潜在的变革影响巨大，不容忽视。

争议的焦点：
• **AI能力的真实性与炒作**：fumeux_fume认为AI被过度炒作，而kristel100则强调其作为辅助工具的价值。
• **与产业合作的利弊**：hbartab和senderista关注与商业公司合作带来的控制权丧失和利益输送问题。

总体来看，讨论围绕AI技术的能力、应用前景、与产业合作的风险以及公共投资的合理性展开。

Q&A with Jason Pruet
A conversation about AI for science with Jason Pruet, Director of the Laboratoryâs National Security AI Office.
March 31, 2025
Kyle Dickman
Download a print-friendly version of this article.
Jason Pruet is working with teams across the Laboratory to help prepare for a future in which artificial intelligence will reshape the landscape of science and security. Five years ago, he viewed AI as just another valuable tool, but because of recent advances in the power of large AI models, Pruet now believes AI will be broadly disruptive. He no longer views the technology as just a tool, but as a fundamental shift in how scientists approach problems and make discoveries. The global race humanity is now in is about how to harness the technologyâs potential while mitigating its harms.
1663:
Â This year, the Lab invested more in AI-related work than at any point in history. Youâve spoken about government investment in AI in terms of returning to a postâWorld War II paradigm of science for the public good. Can you expand on that?
JP:
Â Before World War II, the government wasnât really involved in science the way we think of it today. But after WWII, Vannevar Bush, a key figure behind the Manhattan Project, laid the groundwork for permanent government support of science and engineering. Iâm paraphrasing here, but he had this beautiful quote where he said, âJust as itâs been the policy of the government to keep the frontiers of exploration open for everyone, so itâs the policy of the government that the frontiers of knowledge are open for everyone.â
That uniquely American idea helped build the American Century. After the war, Los Alamos leadership realized that the future of security and science depended on the ability to study energetic particles and nuclear reactions. The problem was that no university could do it because they didnât have the means to build these giant machines. And the Lab couldnât do it without the support of the universities, so they made a deal where the Atomic Energy Commission would pay for these giant facilities, like the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center. Without that kind of infrastructure, the country had no credible way of being a scientific superpower anymore.Â
For a variety of reasons, government support for big science has been eroding since then. Now, AI is starting to feel like the next great foundation for scientific progress. Big companies are spending billions on large machines, but the buy-in costs of working at the frontiers of AI are so high that no university has the exascale-class machines needed to run the latest AI models. Weâre at a place now where we, meaning the government, can revitalize that pact by investing in the infrastructure to study AI for the public good.
1663:
Â Thatâs a fascinating parallel. You mentioned the massive infrastructure required for cutting-edge AI research. Is that something universities can collaborate on with Los Alamos?
JP:
Â Exactly. Part of what weâre doing with the Labâs machines, like Venadoâwhich has 2500 GPUsâis giving universities access to that scale of computing. The scale is just completely different. A typical university might have 50 or 100 GPUs.
Right now, for example, we have partnerships with the University of California, the University of Michigan, and many other universities where researchers can tap into this infrastructure. Thatâs something we want to expand on. Having university collaboration will be critical if the Department of Energy is going to have a comprehensive AI program at scale that is focused on national security and energy dominance.Â
1663:
Â What changed in the last few years to enable this rapid progress? Is it just bigger models, or is there something else at play?
JP:
Â One of the biggest shifts came from a 2017 paper called âAttention Is All You Need,â written by a small group of Google researchers. This paper introduced the transformer architecture, which allowed for a huge leap in how we could scale AI models. It turns out that the bigger the model, the better it performs. Transformers also allow for mixing different types of informationâtext, images, equationsâall within a single framework.Â
1663:
Â Has your perspective on AI shifted since the development of the transformer model?
JP:
Â Definitely. There was a time when I wouldnât have advocated for government investment in AI at the scale weâre seeing now. But the weight of the evidence has become overwhelming. Large modelsâ âfrontier modelsââhave shown such extraordinary capabilities with recent advances in areas as diverse as hypothesis generation, mathematics, biological design, and complex multiphysics simulations. The potential for transformative impact is too significant to ignore.Â
1663:
Â Can you describe where we are on the trajectory of AI development?
JP:

data.author: mfiguiere

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在医疗诊断和治疗中的应用及其争议

不同观点：
• **支持AI在医疗中的应用**：
  - [programmertote] 认为AI可以在常见病的诊断和治疗中发挥作用，特别是在医疗费用高昂的情况下，AI有可能降低患者的成本。他以自身经历为例，指出简单的病情可以通过AI或自我研究解决，而不必支付高额的医生咨询费。
  - [pants2] 分享了自己使用AI（o3模型）进行健康管理的积极体验，认为AI能提供准确的诊断和有效的治疗建议。
  - [mrcwinn] 也表示通过AI得到了有帮助的诊断建议，对长期未确诊的伤病有了新的希望。

• **反对或担忧AI在医疗中的应用**：
  - [imiric] 强烈反对依赖AI进行医疗诊断，认为AI生成的内容缺乏语义理解，可能导致不准确的健康信息，呼吁对此类应用进行严格监管。
  - [unsupp0rted] 分享了一次负面体验，指出ChatGPT在处理实验室报告时产生了错误的癌症诊断，显示出AI的“幻觉”问题，强调了潜在风险。

• **中立或复杂态度**：
  - [Quenby] 对AI在医疗中的角色持复杂态度，认为AI可能不是为了取代医生，而是作为医生的辅助工具，提供快速的信息和帮助，但这种变化让人感到不确定。

• **关于AI模型的公正性和监管**：
  - [dcreater] 提出模型开发者同时作为基准制定者存在利益冲突的问题，建议由非营利实体或独立的商业实体进行监管。
  - [GuinansEyebrows] 对OpenAI的公正性表示怀疑，认为不应将人类生命的判断权交给工具的制造者。

• **关于诊断模型的实用性和基准测试**：
  - [simianwords] 建议设立专门针对诊断的基准测试，认为诊断是AI最有可能提供帮助的领域，特别是在模式识别方面。
  - [srameshc] 询问Google的Med-PaLM模型是否可以作为比较对象，指出该模型尚未公开。

• **关于模型性能和用户体验**：
  - [Zaheer] 认为Grok模型在测试中的表现被低估，相比其他模型（如gemini、llama等）更优秀。
  - [andy99] 质疑这些测试的现实性，认为商业应用中AI系统通常会加入各种防护措施和预设答案，而非让用户直接与基础模型对话。
  - [kypro] 对“Worst-case HealthBench score at k samples”图表的标签颜色和形状设计提出批评，认为其难以辨认。

补充讨论：
- 评论中还涉及对医疗系统成本的讨论，[programmertote] 对比了美国和缅甸的医疗体系，指出在不同国家获取药物和医疗服务的便利性和成本差异。
- 一些评论者分享了个人使用AI进行健康管理的具体案例，这些实例展示了AI在现实生活中可能的应用和局限性。
- 关于AI模型的“幻觉”问题和基准测试的公正性是另一个值得注意的讨论点，显示出对AI医疗应用的技术和伦理担忧。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对基于LLM（大型语言模型）的语音助手（如Siri替代品）的兴趣、技术实现的可行性及挑战。

不同观点：
• [worldsayshi] 对构建基于Whisper模型的语音助手感兴趣，但实际尝试结果不佳，怀疑是麦克风问题或小模型的性能不足。
• [catapart] 希望有现成的应用程序和用户界面来简化配置和教学过程，但仍对指南提供的帮助表示感谢。
• [rrr_oh_man] 对使用LLM撰写文章的目的提出质疑，不理解为什么需要LLM来写这篇文章。
• [thedeep_mind] 对模型能否在iPhone上顺利运行表示关注，提到在iPhone上运行其他模型时遇到的速度问题影响用户体验。
• [jtr1] 提到Siri现在可以在离线模式下执行一些命令，如设置定时器或提醒，暗示Siri的功能在提升。
• [cadamsdotcom] 质疑苹果为何不直接为前1000种常见用例硬编码处理程序，以提高效率。
• [mrcwinn] 对项目表示赞赏，但未深入讨论技术细节。
• [mystified5016] 质疑苹果是否允许用户替换Siri为其他语音助手，提到Android上曾有类似限制。
• [paul7986] 对Siri的表现不满，期待OpenAI和微软推出能替代iPhone的GPT手机，表达了对创新产品的渴望。
• [caust1c] 认为可以自行构建简单的助手，期待社区能开发出替代Siri的方案，并对技术实现的可能性表示乐观。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是现有技术（如Siri）的性能是否足够好，以及是否有可能通过社区力量开发出更好的替代方案。
• 用户对LLM和语音助手的实际应用场景（如iPhone上的用户体验）有不同的期望和需求。
• 对技术实现（如模型选择、硬件性能、系统权限）的讨论反映出用户在尝试自行构建解决方案时遇到的实际困难和挑战。

data.title: The Acid King (2001)
data.author: udit99
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了威廉·伦纳德·皮卡德（William Leonard Pickard）的经历，他是一位哈佛毕业生，去年在堪萨斯州肖尼县监狱成为引人注目的囚犯。他被指控为全球最繁忙的LSD制造者之一，拥有公斤级生产能力。皮卡德来自旧金山湾区，与60年代的反文化运动有深厚渊源，曾与名人及政界人物交往。他早年涉及毒品制造，并多次入狱，但在90年代转向毒品政策研究，生活似乎步入正轨。然而，他被奥克拉荷马州的戈登·托德·斯金纳背叛，再度卷入LSD制造。皮卡德的案件揭示了LSD制造的隐秘世界，反映了60年代理想主义与90年代物质主义的碰撞。LSD生产主要集中在加州的“酸三角”地区，执法部门多年未破获重大案件。

43941068.article_content:
L
ate last year, a new prisoner arrived at the Shawnee County Jail in Topeka, Kansas — a polite beanstalk of a man from the San Francisco Bay Area who stood out among the petty criminals who make up the majority of Shawnee’s inmate population. He spoke in a rapid whisper, practiced yoga, meditated in his cell and read difficult books on mathematics and physics. Along with his prison blues, he wore sandals with socks. A princely mane of silver hair fell almost to his shoulders.
The man’s name was William Leonard Pickard. A few days before, on November 7th, 2000, the 55-year-old Harvard graduate had been arrested not far from an abandoned Atlas E missile silo outside Topeka and charged with being one of the busiest manufacturers of
LSD
in the world, a chemist with the means to cook up acid by the kilo. If the government’s charges prove true, this would make him one of the high priests of acid manufacture, part of a clandestine fraternity that probably numbers no more than a dozen worldwide.
Acid cookers are notoriously hard to catch. A lab can be set up quickly and broken down easily, and it only takes about ten days to perform a series of complicated chemical reactions that produce a sizable batch of the drug — enough, once diluted and dipped onto blotter paper, for hundreds of thousands of hits. The trickiest part of the process is obtaining the precursor chemical known as ergotamine tartrate, or ET. Heavily regulated in this country, where it is used to treat migraines, ET is often smuggled in from Eastern Europe, where sale of the compound is less restricted.
Acid manufacturing might be one of the last criminal enterprises where those involved are motivated by more than the prospect of making money. Even now, more than three decades on from the Summer of Love, to cook acid is to perform a sacrament, a public service. Members of this small band operate with great stealth and are rarely informed on by their associates, even those facing long prison terms. The Drug Enforcement Administration has not taken down an LSD lab since 1991.
Editor’s picks
The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time
The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far
The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time
The 200 Greatest Singers of All Time
The case of
U.S. v. Pickard
is just the latest, and perhaps final, chapter in the strange and often fantastic tale of William Leonard Pickard and his journey from a privileged boyhood in Atlanta, through the manic, hallucinogenic heart of the 1960s, to the forefront of social-
drugs
research in the 1990s, conducted at some of the nation’s most prestigious universities. Along the way — under various aliases — he crossed paths with such rock stars as Sting, and befriended members of the British House of Lords, State Department officials and the district attorney of San Francisco, Terence Hallinan. He earned a master’s from Harvard’s Kennedy School of Government, where he studied drug trends in the former Soviet Union.
Pickard also has a rap sheet stretching back to his teens and has served two prison terms for manufacturing drugs, including LSD and the rarely seen synthetic mescaline. In recent years, though, his life seemed to come together — he’d fathered a child and had become a serious convert to Buddhism. He had a job at a respected drug-policy think tank, and he planned to attend medical school so he could finally dedicate his life to alleviating the suffering of others. But he had also become bizarrely entwined with — and then, he says, hideously betrayed by — a man named Gordon Todd Skinner, a Porsche-driving pot dealer from Tulsa, Oklahoma, 20 years younger than Pickard.
When Pickard comes to trial, most likely later this year, the proceedings promise to shed light on the dangerous and secret world of LSD manufacturing for the first time in decades. Perhaps greater truths will be revealed, too. In some ways, the story of Leonard Pickard and Todd Skinner is a story about the collision of Sixties idealism with the materialism and pragmatism of the Nineties — Timothy Leary’s America versus Bill Clinton’s, if you will. And its moral will be clear even before the judge calls the court to order: The sweet but easily corruptible dream of the flower-power generation never really stood a chance — but it was fun while it lasted.
The Acid Triangle
Most of the acid consumed in the past 30 years is believed to have been made in temporary basement and warehouse labs
in and around San Francisco’s Bay Area, a part of California drug agents call the Acid Triangle. The last time those agents made a significant (one million hits plus) acid bust, in 1993, they identified a supplier who lived in Bolinas, the northernmost point of the triangle. A supplier, that is — not a chemist. The narcs never located the chemist.

• **对毒品流行趋势的预测**：用户[lukasb]提到Pickard在90年代预测了芬太尼流行，提供了一个关于毒品流行趋势的历史视角。

• **LSD在90年代和2000年代初的可获得性**：用户[empath75]认为人们可能低估了90年代和2000年代初LSD在美国获得的容易程度，分享了自己在高中时期以不到5美元的价格获取LSD的经历。

• **其他相关链接和视频分享**：用户[Deprogrammer9]分享了一个关于"Acid King"的视频链接，用户[e6quisitory]和[linuxguy2]提供了其他相关存档链接和年份信息，丰富了讨论的背景资料。

• **LSD剂量问题**：不同用户对LSD的常规剂量有不同看法，焦点在于20微克是否能被视为一个"剂量"，还是100微克更为准确。

data.title: Toward a Sparse and Interpretable Audio Codec
data.author: cochlear
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种旨在实现稀疏且可解释的音频编码器。现有的音频编码方式（如MP3、Ogg Vorbis及一些神经网络编码器）通常基于块编码，虽然能有效压缩音频，但缺乏直观的可解释性。作者提出的编码器使用基于物理事件的稀疏表示，通过模拟乐器和房间的共振等特性，生成易于解释的音频表示。该方法试图在保持音频质量的同时，提供更直观、稀疏的编码方案。

Title:
Toward a Sparse and Interpretable Audio Codec
Authors:
John Vinyard
View a PDF of the paper titled Toward a Sparse and Interpretable Audio Codec, by John Vinyard
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Most widely-used modern audio codecs, such as Ogg Vorbis and MP3, as well as more recent "neural" codecs like Meta's Encodec or the Descript Audio Codec are based on block-coding; audio is divided into overlapping, fixed-size "frames" which are then compressed. While they often yield excellent reproductions and can be used for downstream tasks such as text-to-audio, they do not produce an intuitive, directly-interpretable representation. In this work, we introduce a proof-of-concept audio encoder that represents audio as a sparse set of events and their times-of-occurrence. Rudimentary physics-based assumptions are used to model attack and the physical resonance of both the instrument being played and the room in which a performance occurs, hopefully encouraging a sparse, parsimonious, and easy-to-interpret representation.

data.title: NASA study reveals Venus crust surprise
data.author: mnem
data.article_summary: 新研究显示，金星的地壳存在令人意外的地质活动。尽管金星没有像地球那样的板块构造和俯冲现象，但其地壳通过变质作用和熔融过程进行循环。研究表明，金星地壳底部因密度增加或温度升高，会发生断裂或熔融，将物质送回地幔，驱动火山活动。金星地壳平均厚度约为40公里，最厚处达65公里。这一发现为了解金星的地质过程和演化提供了新视角。未来的任务，如NASA的DAVINCI和VERITAS任务，将进一步研究这些活动是否仍在进行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：金星的地质特性、科学探索任务的现状以及金星是否可以进行地球化改造。

不同观点：
• kristel100认为金星的地壳运动非常有趣，类似于“简化版”的板块构造，暗示金星的地质活动仍有很多未知。
• perihelions 指出NASA的DAVINCI任务在最新的预算请求中被取消，并提到NASA科学 funding的大幅削减，对未来金星探索表示担忧。
• geuis 对金星上大量火山和缺乏撞击坑的现象感到惊讶，推测金星表面会相对频繁地更新。
• p1mrx 通过引用1995年的NOVA节目，回顾了科学家曾经对金星地壳厚度的不确定性，指出科学认知的进步。

补充讨论：
• WalterBright 提出金星是否可以通过在轨道上放置太阳盾来实现地球化，并对逆转金星的温室效应所需的技术规模进行猜测。
• quotemstr 感叹金星未能成为第二个宜居星球，认为如果行星演化稍有不同，金星和地球本可以都是宜居星球，而火星则因为体积问题从未有希望。
• kgwxd 和 minitoar 以幽默的方式回应了关于金星的讨论，分别表示对“金星地壳惊喜”这一概念的兴趣和调侃。
• ossopite 开玩笑地表示无法从标题判断文章是关于天文学还是美食，增加了讨论的趣味性。

争议焦点：
• 金星地质活动的具体机制及其与地球板块构造的类比存在讨论空间，kristel100和geuis的观点表明金星仍有很多未解之谜。
• NASA金星探索任务的取消（perihelions的观点）引发了对未来金星科学研究的担忧和讨论。

43940172.article_content:
3 min read
NASA Study Reveals Venus Crust Surprise
Melissa Gaskill
May 09, 2025
Article
New details about the crust on Venus include some surprises about the geology of Earth’s hotter twin.
This global view of the surface of Venus is centered at 180 degrees east longitude. Magellan synthetic aperture radar mosaics from the first cycle of Magellan mapping are mapped onto a computer-simulated globe to create this image. Data gaps are filled with Pioneer Venus Orbiter data, or a constant mid-range value. Simulated color is used to enhance small-scale structure. The simulated hues are based on color images recorded by the Soviet Venera 13 and 14 spacecraft.
NASA/JPL-Caltech
New details about the crust on Venus include some surprises about the geology of Earth’s hotter twin, according to new NASA-funded research that describes movements of the planet's crust.
Scientists expected the outermost layer of Venus’ crust would grow thicker and thicker over time given its apparent lack of forces that would drive the crust back into the planet’s interior. But the paper,
published
in Nature Communications, proposes a crust metamorphism process based on rock density and melting cycles.
Earth’s rocky crust is made up of massive plates that slowly move, forming folds and faults in a process known as plate tectonics. For example, when two plates collide, the lighter plate slides on top of the denser one, forcing it downward into the layer beneath it, the mantle. This process, known as subduction, helps control the thickness of Earth’s crust. The rocks making up the bottom plate experience changes caused by increasing temperature and pressure as it sinks deeper into the interior of the planet. Those changes are known as metamorphism, which is one cause of volcanic activity.
In contrast, Venus has a crust that is all one piece, with no evidence for subduction caused by plate tectonics like on Earth, explained Justin Filiberto,
deputy chief
of NASA’s Astromaterials Research and Exploration Science Division at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston and a co-author on the paper. The paper used modeling to determine that its crust is about 25 miles (40 kilometers) thick on average and at most 40 miles (65 kilometers) thick.
“That is surprisingly thin, given conditions on the planet,” said Filiberto. “It turns out that, according to our models, as the crust grows thicker, the bottom of it becomes so dense that it either breaks off and becomes part of the mantle or gets hot enough to melt.” So, while Venus has no moving plates, its crust does experience metamorphism. This finding is an important step toward understanding geological processes and evolution of the planet.
“This breaking off or melting can put water and elements back into the planet’s interior and help drive volcanic activity,” added Filiberto. “This gives us a new model for how material returns to the interior of the planet and another way to make lava and spur volcanic eruptions. It resets the playing field for how the geology, crust, and atmosphere on Venus work together.”
The next step, he added, is to gather direct data about Venus' crust to test and refine these models. Several upcoming missions, including NASA’s
DAVINCI
(Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) and
VERITAS
(Venus Emissivity, Radio Science, InSAR, Topography, and Spectroscopy) and, in partnership with ESA (European Space Agency),
Envision
, aim to study the planet’s surface and atmosphere in greater detail. These efforts could help confirm whether processes like metamorphism and recycling are actively shaping the Venusian crust today—and reveal how such activity may be tied to volcanic and atmospheric evolution.
“We don’t actually know how much volcanic activity is on Venus,” Filiberto said. “We assume there is a lot, and research says there should be, but we’d need more data to know for sure.”
Melissa Gaskill

data.title: Interagency Grizzly Bear Committee
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 《Be Bear Aware》文章简要介绍了保护灰熊及其栖息地的相关信息。主要内容包括：提高公众在灰熊活动区域的自我保护意识，避免让熊因食物引诱靠近人类；提供教育资源，帮助人们了解灰熊和如何防范熊的袭击；推广防熊产品，以减少人熊冲突；以及通过跨部门合作保护灰熊及其栖息地。文章还提到 Interagency Grizzly Bear Committee (IGBC) 近40年来在灰熊恢复和保护方面的努力，包括政策协调、研究和宣传等。此外，文章列出了多个即将召开的会议和相关新闻，并提供了实用的安全建议和资源链接。

43945545.article_summary: 《Be Bear Aware》文章简要介绍了保护灰熊及其栖息地的相关信息。主要内容包括：提高公众在灰熊活动区域的自我保护意识，避免让熊因食物引诱靠近人类；提供教育资源，帮助人们了解灰熊和如何防范熊的袭击；推广防熊产品，以减少人熊冲突；以及通过跨部门合作保护灰熊及其栖息地。文章还提到 Interagency Grizzly Bear Committee (IGBC) 近40年来在灰熊恢复和保护方面的努力，包括政策协调、研究和宣传等。此外，文章列出了多个即将召开的会议和相关新闻，并提供了实用的安全建议和资源链接。

data.title: Can you trust that permission pop-up on macOS?
data.author: nmgycombinator
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Mac电脑上新发现并修复的一个安全漏洞（CVE-2025-31250），该漏洞允许应用程序A伪造权限提示，使其看似来自应用程序B，而用户的同意响应却应用于应用程序C。此漏洞存在于macOS的TCC（隐私权限控制）系统中，未修复前，任何能够发送XPC消息到tccd进程的应用都可能利用此漏洞。文章还提到Apple Events这一古老的进程间通信技术，虽然源自1993年的Classic Mac OS时代，但至今仍用于macOS的自动化操作。自macOS Mojave 10.14起，发送Apple Events需要用户通过TCC授权，这与该漏洞的机制相关。修复前，攻击者可借此绕过权限系统，进行潜在的恶意操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：macOS的安全性和权限系统的有效性及用户体验问题

不同观点：
• [xp84] 认为macOS频繁弹出要求输入管理员密码的对话框是一个糟糕的设计，容易被恶意软件模仿，建议采用其他方式（如菜单栏图标或像Windows一样的安全屏幕）来替代。
• [cypherpunks01] 建议通过将应用安装在用户目录下并使用非管理员账户来减少权限请求的干扰，并提到Pareto Security应用推荐这种做法。
• [nmgycombinator] 讨论了macOS某些版本中未修补的漏洞问题，并对Apple未在所有发布版本中包含补丁表示困惑。
• [kristel100] 提到“权限疲劳”现象，用户习惯性点击“允许”以完成工作，建议采用分层的信任模型而不是二元提示。
• [muppetman] 通过对比苹果曾经的广告嘲讽Windows Vista的权限问题，指出自己的Mac现在也有类似甚至更严重的问题。
• [Alex_001] 认为macOS的TCC系统（隐私保护机制）虽然看似坚固，但实际上可能通过数据库操作绕过，提出需要重新思考权限信任的执行方式。
• [nottorp] 表示自己成功拒绝了Mac OS弹出的Chrome访问蓝牙的请求，认为权限系统有时是有效的。
• [lapcat] 认为TCC系统从一开始就是一个“纸牌屋”，只对合法开发者造成障碍，却无法阻止恶意软件，并质疑Apple工程师对技术的理解。
• [sefrost] 提到Slack在Mac上反复弹出要求安装helper tool的提示，IT部门也无法解释，担心存在被利用的风险。
• [silvestrov] 指出Apple花费了一年时间才发布某个漏洞的补丁，认为时间过长。
• [pier25] 提到Adobe Creative Cloud即使在系统设置中禁止后台进程仍会运行，质疑其行为。
• [commandersaki] 赞赏某研究人员的成果和演示。
• [Jerry2] 关心研究人员是否因其工作获得了奖励。
• [zoomTo125] 认为Apple花费近一年时间发布补丁，令人失望，并对其他厂商的表现更加不抱希望。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于macOS权限系统的安全性和用户体验之间的平衡问题。一些用户认为频繁的权限提示不仅打扰工作，还可能导致用户忽视真正的安全威胁（如“权限疲劳”现象）。
• 另一个值得注意的点是Apple在修补漏洞方面的速度和效率问题，有用户认为其反应较慢，导致系统安全风险增加。
• 讨论中也涉及了具体操作建议，如通过将应用安装在用户目录下和使用非管理员账户来减少权限请求干扰，并提供了Pareto Security应用的参考。

43966089.article_content:
Introduction
It's time to update your Macs again! This time, I'm not burying the lede.
CVE-2025-31250
, which was patched in today's releases of macOS Sequoia 15.5 et al., allowed for…
…any
Application A
to make macOS show a permission consent prompt…
…appearing as if it were coming from any
Application B
…
…with the results of the user's consent response being applied to any
Application C.
These did not have to be different applications. In fact, in most normal uses, they would all likely be the same application. Even a case where Applications B and C were the same but different than Application A would be relatively safe (if somewhat useless from Application A's perspective). However, prior to this vulnerability being patched, a lack of validation allowed for Application B (the app the prompt
appears
to be from) to be different than Application C (the
actual
application the user's consent response is applied to).
Spoofing these kinds of prompts is not exactly new. In fact,
the HackTricks wiki has had a tutorial on how to perform a similar trick on their site for a while.
However, their method requires:
the building of an entire fake app in a temporary directory,
the overriding of a shortcut on the Dock, and
the simple hoping that the user clicks on the (now) fake shortcut.
This vulnerability requires
none of the above.
TCC
As I explained in
my first ever article on this site,
TCC is the core permissions system built into Apple's operating systems. It is used by sending messages to the
tccd
daemon (or rather, by using functions in the private
TCC
framework). The framework is a private API, so developers don't call the functions directly (instead, public API's call the functions under-the-hood as needed). However, all this wrapping cannot hide the fact that the control mechanism is still simply sending messages to the daemon.
The daemon uses Apple's public (but proprietary)
XPC API
for messaging (specifically the lower-level dictionary-based API). Prior to this vulnerability being patched, any app with the ability to send XPC messages to
tccd
could send it a specifically-crafted message that, as described above, would make it display a permission prompt as if it were from one app but then apply the user's response to a completely separate app. But how was this possible, and was it even hard? Before I answer these questions, we need to detour into what will, at first, seem like a completely unrelated topic.
Apple Events
What are Apple Events?
Apple Events
are a method of inter-process communication on macOS. As of writing, if you
search
site:developer.apple.com "apple events"
on Google,
one of the very first results will likely be
this PDF document titled
Introduction to Apple Events
.
Skimming through this PDF, you could be forgiven for thinking the contents are at all relevant to modern-day programming. You might find it strange that it starts at Chapter 3, but you may then
search and find the other PDFs that comprise the book.
Looking closer at the book, you might start to get confused at some of the code snippets. It's not until looking closer that you realize…
some of this code is Pascal.
You may then hurriedly search the name of the book and find
an Amazon listing
that includes the publication date:
January 1, 1993
. This is an old book. It predates Mac OS X, and is actually from the era prior (now retroactively known as
Classic Mac OS
). So wait, if this protocol is that old, why am I talking about it now, in 2025, in the context of modern macOS?
The situation I described above happened to me as I was searching for resources on Apple Events. I was looking into the protocol because really… Apple Events are
still
part of macOS. While the new kernel introduced with Mac OS X required the technology to be re-architected, the concept and general use still exists to this day.
The most common use-case for Apple events today is automation (telling a app to perform a specific action or set of actions). This can be scripted through the use of Apple's
Open Scripting Architecture.
The primary language used for these scripts is
AppleScript,
but
JavaScript can also be used.
This is similar to the
Windows Script Host
on Windows. And, like on Windows,
this scripting has been used as a vector for malware.
Apple Events and TCC
So what does this have to do with TCC? Well,
as of macOS Mojave 10.14, the sending of Apple Events by an app requires specific user consent via TCC.
However, attempting to add Apple Events to TCC likely posed a challenge to Apple. Note that much of the following is speculation and I don't want to have to dig up old versions of TCC to validate my theories. However, I do believe they are likely fairly accurate.
As I explained in my previous article, TCC stores user consent results in an SQLite database file located at
[User Home  Folder]/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db
. While it might seem strange to have such sensitive data stored out in the open, this file (and the directory containing i

data.title: How to title your blog post or whatever
data.author: cantaloupe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何为博客文章或其他内容拟定标题。作者建议将标题视为“分类器”，目标是吸引合适的受众点击，同时避免吸引不合适的受众导致负面反馈。好的标题应向目标读者传递强烈信号，确保那些会喜欢内容的人点击，而避免让不喜欢的人浪费时间。作者强调，标题不仅要反映主题，还要体现风格和语气。对于已有名气的作者，标题选择可能更灵活，但对于大多数人，模仿这种策略并不明智。此外，直接将结论放入标题可能引发误解和争议，需谨慎使用。最后，作者提到技术并未解决内容传播问题，社交媒体实际上限制了内容的传播。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：标题设计及其在不同平台上的影响

不同观点：
• [boznz] 认为点击诱饵型标题（如"所有最好的程序员都知道这个..."或"突破可能使核聚变成现实..."）无论内容如何，都会被直接忽略。他希望有办法屏蔽这些标题，因为它们往往出现在YouTube或Reddit的首页。作为作者，他也指出标题或封面图片如果与读者期望不符，可能会导致差评，进而影响算法推荐。

• [tibbar] 认为在Hacker News上，好的标题比内容更重要。一个能引发讨论的标题更容易获得关注和上前页。他指出，如果标题能引发读者联想他们想讨论的相关话题，那么即便内容不足，标题本身也能带来高参与度。

• [sam_lowry_] 基于多年管理社区网站和研究标题的经验，分享了多种标题优化技巧，包括使用预过滤机制、自动通知修改、A/B测试等。最终，他选择取消标题，直接从正文前几句话生成标题，以此强迫用户更深入地思考内容。

• [MattBearman] 提到其YouTuber使用非传统标题模式（如"隔热你的露营车，或只是看着我做"），这种标题风格独特且引人注意。

• [billyp-rva] 认为社交媒体平台通过优化参与度，故意将用户留在平台内，而不是让用户轻易访问外部内容。这种做法导致标题和链接的呈现受到限制。

• [andy99] 对"我做了一个..."这种标题前缀表示不满，认为这种标题过于自我中心，没有突出作品本身。

• [eCa] 强调制作高质量内容比迎合多数人喜好更重要，反对为了吸引点击而妥协内容质量。

• [cosmicgadget] 分享其标题创作流程：先写内容，再根据内容创建标题，并依靠简短描述提供清晰的内容预览。

• [turnsout] 认为带有"或 whatever"这种轻松语气的标题更能吸引人点击，但警告不要滥用这种技巧。

• [amw-zero] 喜欢随意命名内容，认为只要内容好，人们就会找到它，不太在意标题的精确性。

• [paulpauper] 认为负面关注不一定是坏事，有些人会因为反对内容而分享，从而带来更多流量和读者。

补充讨论：
• 不同平台对标题的依赖程度和优化策略存在差异，如YouTube、Reddit、Hacker News等。
• 标题在吸引点击和内容真实性之间的平衡是一个争议焦点，部分人认为点击诱饵标题有害，而另一些人则认为这是有效的策略。
• 自动生成标题和预过滤机制在管理标题质量中的应用和效果被提及，展示了技术在标题优化中的作用。
• 讨论中涉及SEO（搜索引擎优化）和算法推荐对内容可见性的影响，强调标题在这些系统中的重要性。

How to title your blog post or whatever
How to title your blog post or whatever
May 2025
Comments at
substack
,
lemmy
.
So you’ve made a thing. I’ll pretend it’s a blog post, though it doesn’t really matter. If people read your thing, some would like it, and some wouldn’t.
You should try to make a good thing, that many people would like. That presents certain challenges. But our subject today is only how to give your thing a
title
.
My advice is: Think of the title as “classifier”.
When people see the title, some are likely to click on it and some won’t. Abstractly speaking, the title adds a second dimension to the above figure:
A title has two goals. First, think of all the people in the world who, if they clicked on your thing, would finish it and love it. Ideally, those people would click. That is, you want there to be people in the like + click region:
Other people will hate your thing. It’s fine, some people hate everything. But if they click on your thing, they’ll be annoyed and tell everyone you are dumb and bad. You don’t want that. So you
don’t
want people in the hate + click region.
I find it helpful to think about all title-related issues from this perspective.
Everyone is deluged with content. Few people will
hate
your thing, because very few will care enough to have any feelings about it at all.
The good news is that it’s a big world and none of us are that unique. If you make a thing that
you
would love, then I guarantee you at least 0.0001% of other people would love it too. That’s still 8000 people! The problem is finding them.
That’s hard. Because—you don’t like most things, right? So you start with a strong prior that most things are bad (for you). Life is short, so you only click on things when there’s a very strong signal they’ll be good (for you).
Say you write a post about concrete. Should you call it, “My favorite concrete pozzolanic admixtures”, even though 99.9% of people have no idea what pozzolanic means? Well, think of the people who’d actually like your thing. Do
they
know? If so, use “pozzolanic”. That gives a strong signal to Concrete People: “Hey! This is for you! And you
know
I’m not lying about that, because I’ve driven away all the noobs.”
So ideally you’re aiming for something like this:
Be careful imitating famous people. If Barack Obama made a thing called “Thoughts on blockchain”, everyone would read it, because the implicit title is “Thoughts on blockchain,
by Barack Goddamn Obama
”. Most of the titles you see probably come from people who have some kind of established “brand”. If you don’t have that, you probably don’t want to choose the same kind of titles.
The title isn’t just about the subject. I called this post, “How to title your blog post
or whatever
” partly because I hope some of this applies to other things beyond blog posts. But mostly I did that because it signals that my style is breezy and informal. I think people really underrate this.
Some people choose clever punny titles. If you have a big audience that reads all your things, then your title doesn’t need to be a good classifier. I’m not in that situation, but I sometimes find a pun so amusing that I can’t resist.
“Fahren-height”
was worth it.
“Taste games”
was not.
Traditional advice says that you should put your main “message” in the title. I have mixed feelings about that. On the one hand, it provides a lot of signal. On the other hand, it seems to get people’s hackles up. The world is full of bad things that basically pick a conclusion and ignore or distort all conflicting evidence. If you’re attempting to be fair or nuanced, putting your conclusion in the title might signal that you’re going to be a typical biased/bad thing. It will
definitely
lead to lots of comments “refuting” you from people who didn’t read your thing.
Putting your conclusion in the title may also ruin your “story”. Though you should ask: Do the people who’d like your thing really care about your story?
A difficult case is things that create new “labels”. Sometimes there’s an idea floating around, and we need someone to make a canonical thing with a Name. To serve that role, the thing’s title needs to be that name. This presents a trade-off. A post titled
“The Waluigi Effect”
is great for people who want to know what that is, but terrible for everyone else.
For the best
title
ever I nominate,
“I’m worried about Chicago”
. It doesn’t look fancy, but do you see how elegantly it balances all the above issues?
You’d think that, by 2025, technology would have solved the problem of things getting to people. I think it’s the opposite. Social media is optimized to keep people engaged and does not want people leaving the walled garden. Openly prohibiting links would cause a revolt, so instead they go as close as people will tolerate. Which, it turns out, is pretty close.
Boring titles are OK. I know that no one will click on
“Lin
43964620.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何为博客文章或其他内容拟定标题。作者建议将标题视为“分类器”，目标是吸引合适的受众点击，同时避免吸引不合适的受众导致负面反馈。好的标题应向目标读者传递强烈信号，确保那些会喜欢内容的人点击，而避免让不喜欢的人浪费时间。作者强调，标题不仅要反映主题，还要体现风格和语气。对于已有名气的作者，标题选择可能更灵活，但对于大多数人，模仿这种策略并不明智。此外，直接将结论放入标题可能引发误解和争议，需谨慎使用。最后，作者提到技术并未解决内容传播问题，社交媒体实际上限制了内容的传播。

• [tibbar] 认为在Hacker News上，好的标题比内容更重要。一个能引发讨论的标题更容易获得关注和上前页。他指出，如果标题能引发读者联想他们想讨论的相关话题，那么即便内容不足，标题本身也能带来高参与度。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub项目管理工具及其功能完善性

不同观点：
• Jerrygoyal认为GitHub的项目功能已经解决了他遇到的问题，暗示GitHub现有工具能有效满足项目管理需求。
• Rokkamokka支持GitHub项目工具，但也提到他们在工作中自行开发了一个类似的仪表板工具，用来跟踪团队的审查状态，暗示GitHub缺乏类似的内置功能是个错失的机会。
• Dvektor对该想法表示赞同，并指出当前公共实例上存在TLS证书问题，显示出对功能实现细节的关注，同时表示会持续关注项目进展。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了自行开发工具的实践，反映出部分用户可能需要更个性化的功能，而GitHub默认功能未能完全满足这些需求。
• 存在技术问题（如TLS证书问题）也被提及，表明用户对工具的稳定性和可用性有一定期望。
• 总体上，争议焦点在于GitHub是否充分提供了用户所需的项目管理和跟踪功能，部分用户认为有改进空间。

data.title: What if humanity forgot how to make CPUs?
data.author: Tabular-Iceberg
data.article_summary: 文章提到在x.com网站上，一些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能会导致问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序，然后重试以解决潜在的故障。文章提醒用户不必担心，可以尝试再次访问网站。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如果人类失去制造CPU的能力，未来会怎样？

不同观点：
• **对失去CPU制造能力的质疑**：  
  - **palmotea**：如果无法制造CPU，也不可能维持私人网络或卫星连接，因为这些也需要设备支持。同时，如果无法制造CPU，光学媒体驱动器的生产也无法持续。
  - **0xTJ**：30年内不可能失去制造CPU的能力，至少能恢复到20世纪70年代中期的生产水平。对MC68000处理器寿命达10,000年的说法表示怀疑。

• **制造CPU的挑战**：  
  - **mahirsaid**：更大的问题在于如何制造生产CPU的机器，这是当前行业的关键挑战，尤其是如果唯一掌握该技术的公司消失的话。
  - **PaulKeeble**：由于大部分技术知识掌握在少数私人公司手中，如果这些公司倒闭，可能无法轻易复制其成果，尤其是在科学和工程领域。

• **软件和基础设施的影响**：  
  - **CuriousRose**：如果无法制造新CPU，可能会促使更高效软件的开发，迫使程序员优化代码，类似于20世纪80年代的情形。
  - **asciimov**：问题不仅在于CPU，还在于基础设施如电力、制造业和医疗保健中的重要芯片。

• **替代方案和未来展望**：  
  - **vardump**：应研究如何用简单输入小规模生产芯片，这不仅对地球重要，对殖民其他星球也有帮助。
  - **myth_drannon**：可能回归使用6502处理器，只需更多时间优化代码。
  - **datadrivenangel**：虽然会有一段困难时期，但有人会为了经济利益快速恢复旧芯片的生产。

• **其他讨论**：  
  - **trollbridge**：对“忘记如何制造CPU”也包括忘记如何制造机械硬盘、闪存和其他芯片感到困惑。
  - **andsoitis**：质疑人类忘记如何制造CPU的前提条件是什么。
  - **roxolotl**：关注电子设备的使用寿命，如开关和电视在10年内是否会失效。
  - **FrankWilhoit**：认为人类会忘记很多事情。
  - **Vilian**：希望JavaScript也被遗忘，认为这是一件好事。

补充讨论：评论中还涉及了对具体技术细节的争论，如IC寿命和历史发展时间线的准确性，以及对当前技术知识保存和传播方式的担忧。

data.title: Memories: Edinburgh ML to Standard ML
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要回顾了Standard ML的发展历史及其与Caml的分裂。作者Dave MacQueen等人编写了《Standard ML历史》一文。作者回顾了ML语言的早期发展，尤其是Edinburgh ML在定理证明方面的创新，但因ML代码通过Lisp解释导致执行缓慢。通过λ-lifting和优化currying等技术改进，ML性能显著提升。随着ML under UNIX的出现，ML语言面临分裂风险，Robin Milner因此推动标准化工作。在标准化的过程中，不同团队对ML的特性存在分歧，特别是关于非线性模式和局部声明语法等问题。最终，Standard ML的模块化方案成为争议点，尽管起初被认为复杂，但如今OCaml的模块与Standard ML相似。文章还提到ML的语法受ISWIM影响，具有一定随意性。

43967243.article_content:
Machine Logic
At the junction of computation, logic and mathematics
Memories: Edinburgh ML to Standard ML
05 Oct 2022
[
general
Robin Milner
Standard ML
memories
]
Dave MacQueen (with Robert Harper and John Reppy) has written a 100-page
History of Standard ML
.
Here I offer my brief, personal and utterly subjective impressions of its early days,
up to the deeply unfortunate schism that created
what was then called
Caml
.
Standard ML
was a tragic missed opportunity.
But even today there are still several viable
implementations:
Poly/ML
,
SML/NJ
,
Moscow ML
and
MLton
.
They are substantially compatible because the language was defined by an operational semantics.
It’s sad that well into the 21st Century, Computer Science has so regressed that people no longer see the point of distinguishing
between a programming language and its implementation.
Edinburgh ML
The
previous post
describes how Edinburgh LCF created a distinctive new architecture for theorem proving based on a
programmable metalanguage
, namely ML.
Execution was slow because ML code was translated into Lisp to be interpreted there.
Gérard Huet modified the compiler to emit the Lisp in source form to be compiled, but it ran no faster.
As he informed me, every ML function was represented by
a closure containing a quoted LAMBDA-expression,
and the Lisp compiler cannot compile S-expressions into
executable machine instructions.
When Gérard sent the LCF sources back to me,
I managed to solve this problem
by what is now called
λ-lifting
:
by extracting the closure bodies and declaring them as top-level Lisp functions.
Currying also required optimisation.
As a curried function receives its arguments
it returns a succession of trivial closures;
by compiling additional functions to cover the common case of
a curried function being applied to multiple arguments at once,
this wasteful computation could be eliminated.
I don’t remember running any benchmarks, but I surely did.
Mike Gordon reported a speedup by
a factor of twenty
.
ML was finally usable. But the arrival of
Luca Cardelli
’s
“ML under UNIX” changed everything. It was a rich, powerful language
with native-code generation and good
performance. The danger that ML could splinter as Lisp did
prompted Robin Milner to launch his standardisation effort.
The fateful meeting
Dave’s account lists a series of meetings convened by Robin
in order arrive at a consensus for Standard ML.
I no longer have a clear recollection.
The meeting sketched below may have happened in June 1984 or April 1983.
A colleague who went in my stead to a much later ML meeting
remarked that it was “hard to hear over the sound of clashing egos”.
The delegate sent by Gérard to represent Projet Formel was not like that. Guy Cousineau was quiet and gentle;
he put forward Gérard’s proposals and they were all shot down.
I can’t remember them all but recall the following:
“non-linear patterns”, i.e. repeating a pattern variable would be permitted and denoted an equality test
a
where
syntax for local declarations
more generally, to keep the syntax closer to Edinburgh ML
Clearly Dave and Gérard had different visions of ML, and while
Gérard would have fiercely pressed his demands,
he wasn’t there and Dave got his way.
I actually think he was right on all counts: non-linear patterns
are harder to implement and
only useful for a few little examples, while
where
would
not only be redundant but would introduce new scoping issues
exactly when we were striving for a syntax where all scopes
were delimited. But for the sake of harmony it would have been far
better to have conceded some of those points.
As somebody told me at the time, “the French did not get anything they wanted”. We know how that ended.
Standard ML modules
The other point of contention was
Dave’s module proposal
with its structures, signatures and functors.
(Some insights by
Mads Tofte
.)
Roughly speaking,
structures
(which contain the executable code) correspond to values and
satisfy
signatures
, which correspond to types and allow a module
to be specified without reference to any implementation.
Functors
provide a way to define structures that take other structures as parameters.
In 1984, Dave’s proposal seemed ludicrously baroque to simple-minded souls like myself and seemingly to the French group too.
As I recall, Caml launched with basic modules that worked with UNIX Makefiles to generate
.o

43967243.article_summary: 这篇文章简要回顾了Standard ML的发展历史及其与Caml的分裂。作者Dave MacQueen等人编写了《Standard ML历史》一文。作者回顾了ML语言的早期发展，尤其是Edinburgh ML在定理证明方面的创新，但因ML代码通过Lisp解释导致执行缓慢。通过λ-lifting和优化currying等技术改进，ML性能显著提升。随着ML under UNIX的出现，ML语言面临分裂风险，Robin Milner因此推动标准化工作。在标准化的过程中，不同团队对ML的特性存在分歧，特别是关于非线性模式和局部声明语法等问题。最终，Standard ML的模块化方案成为争议点，尽管起初被认为复杂，但如今OCaml的模块与Standard ML相似。文章还提到ML的语法受ISWIM影响，具有一定随意性。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大龄技术人员在当前就业市场中的挑战，特别是远程工作、技术技能和AI对就业市场的冲击。

不同观点：
• uberman：虽然对当事人表示同情，但认为他选择住在农村地区且坚持远程工作给自己增加了困难。同时指出，就业市场的权力动态已经改变，建议当事人重新发布被删除的AI相关内容以增加就业机会。
• speedbird：认为当事人给自己设置了太多限制（如仅接受远程工作），建议他调整求职策略，包括可能需要接受薪资下降或角色吸引力降低的现实，甚至可能需要搬家。
• Havoc：对AI导致就业困难的关联性持怀疑态度，认为社会在过去几年发生了变化，导致求职变得更加困难，但并不完全是AI的影响。
• Shorel：不认为AI是主要问题，强调技能匹配的重要性。
• ecshafer：分享了自己的求职经验，建议当事人在当地寻找机会，特别是在国防行业，并提升C、C++和Java技能。
• Padriac：提到在澳大利亚，军事部门的网络和技术岗位招聘薪资优厚，建议当事人考虑这类机会。
• Arnt：指出PHP开发者面临类似于多年前Perl开发者的困境，认为技术单一可能是问题所在。
• RainyDayTmrw：认为当前社会和经济系统极其脆弱，导致就业市场对轻微冲击反应过度。
• YeGoblynQueenne：认为问题在于行业年龄歧视，而不是AI。指出软件行业对大龄员工不友好，特别是男性。
• tetris11：质疑当前经济转型对普通劳动者的影响，特别是如果转向科技封建主义，普通劳动者将何去何从。
• 1attice：呼吁评论者在发表评论时多些同理心，少些自我保护和批判，以建设性的方式提供建议。
• adamc：认为当前社会缺乏对类似问题的解决方案，批评当前政策只利于富人，对普通劳动者缺乏帮助和希望。
• fullstackchris：以讽刺口吻指出AI并未如预期那样解决实际问题，如网页cookie偏好设置的保存。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI是否是导致当事人求职困难的主要原因。部分评论者认为社会和经济变化以及行业年龄歧视是更主要的原因。
• 另一个值得注意的点是地理位置和技能匹配对求职的影响，建议当事人调整求职策略和技能提升。
• 评论中还提到了不同地区（如美国和澳大利亚）的技术岗位机会差异，以及军事和国防行业的招聘机会。
• 最后，一些评论者呼吁更多的同理心和建设性建议，以帮助当事人应对求职挑战。

data.title: Scientists Looking to Leave the U.S. for More Welcoming Environments
data.author: burkaman
data.article_summary: 文章主要报道了在波士顿举行的美国科学促进会（AAAS）年会上，德国德累斯顿工业大学的研究人员Marion Schmidt展示了其在智能手套等领域的最新研究成果。然而，会议讨论的重点却转向了德国提供的职业机会，尤其是由于特朗普政府对科学的打压，许多美国学术精英正在考虑离开美国，可能前往德国等国家。文章提到，特朗普的政策包括削减科研经费、驱逐非美国籍学生以及干预大学招生，这导致哈佛等顶尖大学面临财政危机和法律挑战。同时，美国国家卫生研究院（NIH）等机构的大幅预算削减将对医学研究和经济产生深远影响，可能引发学术人才外流。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧美在科研启动资金、人才吸引力及科研环境方面的比较

不同观点：
• [arcanus] 认为欧洲的科研实验室启动资金比美国少，而这直接影响了人才的流向。他强调启动资金是吸引人才的关键因素。

• [moomin] 认为美国在科学研究领域的领先地位是过去一贯政策环境的产物，并对未来这种领先是否能持续表示担忧。他暗示如果政策环境发生变化，美国可能会失去其优势，并成为未来人们怀念的“黄金时代”。

补充讨论：
• [Am4TIfIsER0ppos] 以讽刺的语气表示，如果有人去美国，可以把护照给他，他想离开当前的环境。这反映出对当前所处地区科研环境的不满。

• [datavirtue] 引用了带有批评性质的言论，暗示美国科研机构过去的行为造成了问题，但没有具体展开。

• [esbranson] 使用讽刺和隐喻（“无知是福，邻家的草更绿”）来评论当前对科研环境的看法，并附上一个标签 #SaveBrainCity，可能是在呼吁保护或改善当前的科研城市或人才环境。

• [sQL_inject] 用幽默的方式批评欧盟科学家薪资较低的问题，暗示即使有好的科研环境，薪资问题可能会导致人才流失。

争议焦点：
- 欧美在科研启动资金和人才吸引力方面的比较是主要争议点。一方认为美国的资金和政策环境更有利于科研发展，另一方则担心这种优势无法持续，并对欧盟的科研环境表示不满或担忧。

总结：评论中主要围绕欧美科研环境的资金、政策、人才吸引力及未来发展潜力展开讨论，其中包含对美国科研领先地位的肯定与隐忧，以及对欧洲科研环境问题的批评与幽默调侃。

Marion Schmidt had actually traveled to one of the most important gatherings of researchers to present recent developments at her university. The annual event held by the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) is one of the most prestigious scientific conferences in the world, with AI researchers, astrophysicists, biologists and others making the pilgrimage to Boston.
Together with her colleagues from the Center for Tactile Internet at the Technical University of Dresden, Schmidt was eager to share their recent results, including smart gloves with the ability to recognize early on the next object a person is likely to grab.
Ultimately, though, says Schmidt, the podium discussion focused less on her research results and more on possible career opportunities in Germany. She says she felt almost like she was at an academic recruiting event: "Young students wanted to know how university studies in Germany work. Professors were asking how they could get an appointment at a university.”
DER SPIEGEL 18/2025
The article you are reading originally appeared in German in issue 18/2025 (April 25th, 2025) of DER SPIEGEL.
SPIEGEL International
Schmidt is the head of communications for TU Dresden and part of the university leadership. She was able to tell a NASA researcher, who was afraid of losing her job as soon as the following week, that five new professorships would soon need to be filled: Together with the German Center for Astrophysics, TU Dresden will be introducing a new course of study. Perhaps she might be interested? Initial contacts have been made.
Might NASA experts soon be coming to Saxony? Will AI researchers be leaving Stanford for Karlsruhe? Boston-based biomedical experts to Bavaria? Some appear to be thinking about it – while others are making concrete plans. This year’s AAAS conference seemed to hint at a potential brain drain – an emigration of academic elites out of the United States.
Many researchers are looking for a new home because the Trump administration has launched a broadside attack on science in the U.S. Undesirable students who do not hold American passports are to be deported.
Students like Mahmoud Khalil, who helped organize pro-Palestinian student protests at Columbia University in New York and who has been accused by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio of undermining U.S. foreign policy. Khalil’s defense attorneys deny the accusation, citing freedom of expression. Or the South Korean Yunseo Chung, who has been living in the United States since she was seven years old and took part in demonstrations.Under Trump’s leadership, Washington is also planning to slash financial support, with universities like Harvard, Columbia and Cornell losing hundreds of millions, perhaps billions, in funding. Some universities, not knowing where the money will come from in the future, have responded with hiring freezes, delayed infrastructure investments and cancelled commitments for doctoral positions.
Harvard University alone stands to lose several billion dollars in federal funding and its academic integrity is at stake. The Trump administration recently demanded that Harvard change its admissions processes and that it share all relevant data with the authorities. In addition, Washington demanded that student rights be curtailed and international students who break the rules be reported to the authorities. Harvard President Alan Garber refused to accept the conditions and instead filed a lawsuit against the government.
Undeterred, Trump doubled down. As a non-profit institution, Harvard enjoys wide-ranging tax privileges. But the White House now wants to have that status reviewed. Were its tax-free status revoked, Harvard could owe billions in taxes on its assets.
Trump is also shutting down the most important source for medical research. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) have a budget of almost $48 billion and send about 80 percent of that total onward to U.S. universities and research institutes in the form of grants.
In early April, though, 1,300 agency employees were laid off and the NIH was ordered to cut $2.6 billion in spending this year. In total, the NIH budget is to be slashed by 35 percent. Other agencies under the aegis of the Department of Health have suffered a similar fate, including the Centers for Disease Control and the Food and Drug Administration.
The consequences will be vast, and they will affect every part of the country. Research doesn’t just produce improved therapies and better medical drugs, it also stimulates the economy. According to a report by United for Medical Research, every dollar of NIH funding produces a profit of $2.56 – a return that stock market investors can only dream of. State funding also guarantees more than 408,000 jobs across the country.
Where are the researchers supposed to go? Some woul

data.article_summary:
本文总结了美国就业与培训管理局发布的截至2025年5月3日的失业保险每周申领报告数据。主要内容包括：

- 2025年5月3日，经季节性调整后的初始失业金申领人数为228,000。
- 此前几周的申领人数分别为：4月26日241,000，4月19日223,000，4月12日216,000，4月5日224,000。
- 数据每周更新，下次发布日期为2025年5月15日。
- 初始申领是失业者在离职后申请失业保险资格的申诉。
- 数据来源为联邦储备经济数据（FRED）系统，由圣路易斯联邦储备银行提供。

此外，文章还提供了相关数据链接和博客建议，帮助用户更好地理解和使用初始申领数据。

不同观点：

• ImJamal则持有不同看法，他认为从过去一年的数据来看，情况已经相对稳定。他提到，与2024年5月的初始数据相比，目前的数字下降了1000，暗示变化是渐进的并且已经有所反映。

补充讨论：
• Havoc强调了时间延迟的问题，特别是关税等政策的影响需要时间才能在消费者层面显现。
• ImJamal的观点基于数据趋势，他认为从长时间跨度来看，当前的变化是持续的，并且已经有显著的下降。
• 争议的焦点在于当前经济混乱的影响是否已经充分反映出来，Havoc倾向于认为影响还在传递过程中，而ImJamal则认为影响已经有所体现。

本文总结了美国就业与培训管理局发布的截至2025年5月3日的失业保险每周申领报告数据。主要内容包括：

- 2025年5月3日，经季节性调整后的初始失业金申领人数为228,000。
- 此前几周的申领人数分别为：4月26日241,000，4月19日223,000，4月12日216,000，4月5日224,000。
- 数据每周更新，下次发布日期为2025年5月15日。
- 初始申领是失业者在离职后申请失业保险资格的申诉。
- 数据来源为联邦储备经济数据（FRED）系统，由圣路易斯联邦储备银行提供。

此外，文章还提供了相关数据链接和博客建议，帮助用户更好地理解和使用初始申领数据。

data.title: Some politicians who share harmful information are rewarded with more clicks
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 该文章指出，研究发现美国州议员通过在社交媒体上分享低可信度信息或使用不文明语言，可以增加其公众 visibility，尤其是在政治紧张时期。研究分析了2020至2021年间近400万条推文和50万条Facebook帖子，发现共和党议员发布低可信度信息更易获得关注，而发布不文明内容则普遍降低 visibility，尤其是极端意识形态的议员。文章担忧社交媒体算法可能无意中鼓励了分裂性和误导性行为，导致公众辩论失真、两极分化加剧，选民难以获得可信信息。未来研究将探讨这些模式是否持续，以及平台政策变化的影响。
